title: A Recipe for the Locker
premise: At Ashgrove Academy, scholarship student Elodie Marchetti keeps her head down until an anonymous group chat called The Locker starts posting predictions that come true with unsettling accuracy. When the chat forecasts a tragedy involving her best friend Priya's final audition, Elodie realizes the predictions are being written by someone inside their circle — and that she herself is the next subject. Uncovering the truth means exposing the grief-fueled vigilante justice of a student who lost a sibling to the school's covered-up hazing scandal, forcing Elodie to choose between protecting her found family and telling a truth that could shatter it. In the end, she testifies before the academy board, the chat is unmasked, and though Priya walks away, Elodie earns her place on stage — and in a rebuilt, honest friendship.
about_author: Sebastian Eriksen is the pen name of a former boarding-school teacher who spent six years watching teenagers keep each other's secrets. They write young adult fiction about the moment loyalty and truth stop being the same thing.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. We meet her survival rules at Ashgrove: invisible, excellent, unremarkable. She navigates a scholarship dinner where wealthy donors gawk, leaning on her quiet friendship with Priya, a music prodigy preparing for the conservatory audition of her life. Emotional beat: the comfort — and loneliness — of staying hidden.

chapters.title: The First Message
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. An unknown number adds her to a group chat called The Locker. The first prediction — a pipe burst flooding the east wing — comes true within hours. Elodie tells no one, telling herself it's a prank. Emotional beat: a cold prickle of wrongness beneath ordinary school life.

chapters.title: Rules of the Chat
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. More predictions land: a cancelled fire drill, a teacher's resignation, a varsity injury. Each arrives with a countdown. Elodie notices the chat knows things only students could know. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into complicity as she reads instead of reporting.

chapters.title: Priya's Audition Clock
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Priya. Priya rehearses obsessively for the Halvorsen Conservatory audition while hiding a stress tremor in her left hand. Elodie promises to be at the audition. Emotional beat: tenderness between friends who keep different kinds of secrets.

chapters.title: The Prediction About Priya
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The Locker posts: 'The violinist won't make it to the stage.' No date, no method. Elodie confronts the chat; it replies with a detail only someone close to Priya would know. Emotional beat: fear arriving like ice water.

chapters.title: Who Else Is In Here
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She quietly inventories the chat's members — all anonymous handles — and cross-references prediction details against who had access: dorm staff, yearbook editors, the theater crew. Suspicion lands uncomfortably close to home. Emotional beat: paranoia reframing every friendly face.

chapters.title: Marcus Knows Something
chapters.summary: Dual POV with Marcus, theater tech and Elodie's reluctant ally. He admits he was added weeks ago and ignored it, ashamed he'd once benefited from a prediction that got him out of trouble. Emotional beat: guilt shared is burden halved — barely.

chapters.title: What Happened to Theo
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Digging through archived school papers, she finds the name Theo Vance — a student injured in an off-book initiation ritual three years ago, quietly settled and scrubbed from record. The timeline matches the chat's first appearance. Emotional beat: the school's rot becoming visible.

chapters.title: The Sister
chapters.summary: POV shift to Wren, revealed to readers but not Elodie: Theo's younger sister, now a senior, who started The Locker not to hurt anyone but to force the school to remember what it buried. Her predictions are leverage built from overheard secrets. Emotional beat: righteous grief hardening into something dangerous.

chapters.title: An Almost Confession
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie corners Wren with circumstantial evidence; Wren deflects brilliantly and turns it around — why does Elodie care more about the school's reputation than Theo's? Emotional beat: doubt planted in Elodie's own motives.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The Locker posts a date: three days before Priya's audition. The prediction sharpens — 'the violinist's hands will fail her.' Elodie suspects sabotage: rosin swapped, strings tampered, or something psychological. Emotional beat: racing clock, thinning air.

chapters.title: Found Family, Fraying
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter across Elodie, Marcus, and Priya. The trio spends a late night in the tech booth, and Elodie nearly tells them everything — but a Locker message pings mid-sentence, quoting her almost-words verbatim. Someone in the room is watching. Emotional beat: intimacy poisoned by surveillance.

chapters.title: The Rosin
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie finds Priya's rosin replaced with a compound that degrades bow grip — proof of physical sabotage, and proof the threat isn't just digital. She swaps it back and says nothing, protecting Priya from panic. Emotional beat: protective lies stacking up.

chapters.title: Wren's Version
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren shows Elodie (anonymously, via the chat) the full record of Theo's injury: photos, a coerced statement, administrators choosing donors over a boy. She argues the audition threat isn't hers — someone else escalated. Emotional beat: sympathy for the devil, or what looks like one.

chapters.title: A Second Author
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Comparing message styles, Elodie confirms two voices in the chat: Wren's leverage game, and a colder hand adding threats Wren never wrote. The escalation began when Wren shared admin access. Emotional beat: the horror of losing control of your own weapon.

chapters.title: The Accusation
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya discovers the tampered rostin — and Elodie's silence about it. Feeling betrayed twice over, she accuses Elodie of choosing secrets over her, echoing how the school chose silence over Theo. Emotional beat: the friendship fracture the blurb promised.

chapters.title: Confession in the Empty Theater
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie finds Wren in the auditorium and gets the whole truth: Wren never intended harm; co-admin Devon Hale — brother of one of Theo's tormentors — twisted the chat to destroy Priya's audition and bury the scandal deeper. Emotional beat: clarity arriving too late to be painless.

chapters.title: Devon's Move
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Elodie and Devon. Devon, cornered, leaks doctored messages framing Wren entirely and schedules his own 'prediction' to come true during auditions. Elodie realizes the only counter is truth told publicly, fast, and together. Emotional beat: resolve replacing fear.

chapters.title: Audition Day
chapters.summary: Ensemble climax, part one. Audition morning: Devon's sabotage triggers, Priya's tremor spikes, and the board convenes an emergency session over the leaked 'evidence.' Elodie walks into the boardroom with Wren beside her and the real archive in hand. Emotional beat: stepping out from hiding for good.

chapters.title: The Truth, Out Loud
chapters.summary: Climax, part two. Elodie testifies — about the chat, the cover-up, her own silences — putting her scholarship on the line. Devon's forgery unravels under timestamp evidence Marcus salvaged. The board suspends him and reopens the Theo Vance inquiry. Emotional beat: costly honesty finally paying its dividend.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Resolution. The academy grants Priya a rescheduled audition; she plays through the tremor and earns her conservatory seat. Wren faces disciplinary consequences but wins the public reckoning Theo deserved. Elodie keeps her place — earned, not granted. Emotional beat: bittersweet victory, grief honored.

chapters.title: A Recipe for the Locker
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Elodie's POV. Weeks later, Elodie and Priya rebuild slowly over shared practice-room hours; Wren, on probation, joins them for Sunday dinners — a found family assembled from wreckage. A new anonymous message appears; Elodie deletes the chat without reading it. Emotional beat: closure chosen, not given.
